events.title: THE AUTHENTICATED COPIES ARE SEALED INTO THE HOUSEHOLD ARCHIVE
events.body: The duplicate set requested by Marcus Claudius Marcellus is completed and checked against the original papers. The scribes preserve the chronology of the records while marking each copy against its corresponding original, and the completed set is sealed with the household archive. The work takes care not to replace the original evidence or alter its wording. A separate notation records who handled the copies and when they were sealed. The archive now contains both the original dossier and an authenticated working duplicate, allowing later requests to be answered without repeatedly handling the principal papers.

events.title: THE OLD BOUNDARY MARKER IS COMPARED WITH THE PURCHASE RECORDS
events.body: The stewards return to the old boundary marker discovered during the previous week's inspection and compare it with the written description of the tract purchased from the neighboring smallholders. Measurements and witness recollections are reviewed together rather than relying on the marker alone. The comparison finds that the marker belongs to an older division of the surrounding land and does not contradict the completed purchase. The result is entered into the estate's property records, reducing the chance that the old marker will later be mistaken for a current boundary. The neighboring parties are not summoned into a confrontation, and the clarification is handled through the household's established administrative procedure.

events.title: A SECOND WITNESS CONFIRMS PART OF THE SMALLHOLDER'S RAID ACCOUNT
events.body: A second local witness comes forward after hearing that the household is preserving the earlier smallholder's account without coercion. The witness confirms part of the route described in the first statement, while also distinguishing what he personally saw from what he later heard from others. The scribes record those distinctions rather than merging the two accounts into a single narrative. The additional testimony does not establish responsibility for the raid, but it strengthens the chronological comparison available to the dossier. Valerius orders both statements retained separately so that their agreements and differences remain visible to anyone examining the record.

events.title: THE SPRING FIELDS DRAW MORE LABOR AS THE NEW TRACT IS FULLY BROUGHT INTO ROTATION
events.body: The newly purchased tract is brought further into the estate's spring rotation as workers complete preparation of the ground and extend ordinary field labor onto the newly incorporated acres. Stewards coordinate the work with existing fields so that labor and stores are not committed beyond the household's practical capacity. Several nearby agricultural workers participate in the seasonal work under the estate's established arrangements, while the stewards continue to keep the newly acquired tract separately identified in the property records until the transition is fully settled. The work increases the productive use of the estate without changing its boundaries. Grain and fodder stores are drawn upon for the expanded operation, and the resulting activity is entered into the household's agricultural records.

events.title: A ROMAN ACKNOWLEDGMENT CONFIRMS RECEIPT OF THE PRESERVED DOSSIER SET
events.body: A further Roman communication reaches the estate acknowledging that the dossier, its chronology, and the authenticated duplicates have been preserved as requested. The communication does not announce a final finding, but it confirms that the records are available for continued examination and that the Roman correspondents understand which copies correspond to the originals. Valerius's scribes attach the acknowledgment to the archive record and preserve it with the previous correspondence. The confirmation closes the immediate administrative exchange surrounding the transmission while leaving the underlying inquiry open. The household therefore retains the complete documentary trail rather than treating the acknowledgment as a conclusion to the matter.

events.title: THE ESTATE'S SPRING ACCOUNTS ARE RECONCILED AFTER A WEEK OF HEAVIER FIELD WORK
events.body: At the week's close, the stewards reconcile the ordinary estate accounts after the increased field activity. The records distinguish labor, provisions, and maintenance from the earlier purchase of the disputed tract, which remains a completed transaction rather than a recurring expense. No extraordinary payment is required, but the expanded agricultural work produces a modest realized return from ordinary estate activity. The stewards enter the receipt into the public operating account and close the week's books with the supporting entries preserved in the household archive.
